title: SCT Temporal Change Detection Report
subtitle: Scalloped Terrain Scarp Retreat Measurement via Sub-pixel Phase Correlation

methodology.pipeline: Sub-pixel phase correlation (COSI-Corr approach, Leprince et al. 2007)

steps.name: CRS Bug Detection
steps.detail: PSP-era JP2 has WKT with standard_parallel_1=0 (wrong); ESP-era has standard_parallel_1=40 (correct). Both images were produced with lat_ts=40 internally — only the metadata label is wrong. Verified by comparing pixel width to RDRCUMINDEX lon range.

steps.name: Coarse Alignment
steps.detail: 4x downsampled NCC template matching (400×400 template in 1600×1600 search area). Found ~500m offset (dcol=1497, drow=1657 px). NCC peak = 0.82.

steps.name: Fine Alignment
steps.detail: Full-resolution 1024×1024 NCC template matching with ±200px search margin. Refined offset by additional (35, -33) px. Total offset: dcol=1532, drow=1624. NCC peak = 0.84.

steps.name: Terrain Classification
steps.detail: Gradient magnitude (Sobel) and local texture (64px window std) used to classify pixels. Stable terrain: low gradient (< 70th pctl) + moderate texture (20th-80th pctl) → 42.5% of image. Scarp edges: high gradient (> 85th pctl) → 15.0% of image.

steps.name: Stable-Terrain Affine Co-registration
steps.detail: 39 tie-points extracted from stable terrain only (NCC > 0.4, stable fraction > 60%, scarp fraction < 15%). RANSAC affine fitting with 0.8px inlier threshold → 11 inliers (33.3%). Final affine model accounts for translation + rotation + scale systematic errors.

steps.name: Full Displacement Measurement
steps.detail: Sliding window phase correlation: 256×256 px chips (64m), 128px step (32m), subpixel parabolic refinement. Affine model subtracted from all measurements. 2025 chips total, 1523 with NCC > 0.5.

methodology.key_innovation: Stable-terrain-only affine registration preserves real displacement signal at scarp edges while removing systematic geometric distortion. This avoids the pitfall of polynomial warping that would absorb the very signal being measured.

affine_model.note: Low inlier ratio suggests possible higher-order distortion beyond affine. Stable terrain noise (1.02m) exceeds registration RMS (0.07m), indicating additional error sources (atmospheric effects, sensor noise, interpolation).

stable_terrain.interpretation: Represents co-registration noise floor. Should be ~0 if registration is perfect.

scarp_terrain.interpretation: Includes both real displacement and co-registration noise.

ks_test.test: H0: scarp and stable distributions are identical

interpretation.primary_finding: Statistically significant (p < 0.001) excess displacement at scarp edges relative to stable terrain, consistent with active scarp retreat.

comparison_to_literature.ratio: ~10-60× lower than Dundas (2015) thermal model prediction
comparison_to_literature.explanation: Several factors: (1) Dundas model assumes active sublimation at favorable thermal conditions — our 8-year average includes quiescent periods. (2) The 44°N latitude is at the equatorward margin of active SCT evolution where retreat may be slower. (3) Co-registration noise (1.02m stable terrain) limits sensitivity — real retreat may be partially masked. (4) Phase correlation measures horizontal displacement, while thermal contraction/sublimation may produce predominantly vertical (subsidence) changes invisible to planimetric analysis.

caveats: RANSAC inlier ratio (33%) is low — higher-order distortion likely present beyond affine model
Stable terrain noise floor (1.02m) is high relative to measured signal (0.38m excess)
Only one temporal pair analyzed — results not yet validated against independent pairs
Planimetric measurement cannot capture vertical subsidence, only lateral scarp migration
64m chip size may average out localized scarp retreat occurring at finer scales
interpretation.significance: Even at the current noise level, the detection of statistically significant differential displacement between scarp and stable terrain demonstrates the viability of sub-pixel phase correlation for measuring SCT evolution on Mars. With improved co-registration (higher-order distortion correction) or additional temporal pairs for stacking, detection sensitivity could reach 0.01 m/Mars-yr.
